reason: The passage from 2 Kings 11 focuses on the overthrow of an illegitimate, tyrannical queen (Athaliah) and the restoration of the young legitimate heir (Jehoash, age 7) under the guidance of the priest Jehoiada. While the narrative presents a model of proper succession, divine covenant, and priestly authority, it does not demonstrate humility in the face of criticism as a leadership virtue. Athaliah, who faces opposition, responds with defiance rather than humility and is executed. The young Jehoash is too young to demonstrate any leadership qualities. Jehoiada the priest, while righteous and faithful, acts authoritatively in orchestrating the coup without himself facing criticism. The passage presents a contrast between wicked, prideful rule (Athaliah) and legitimate, covenant-based restoration (Jehoash/Jehoiada), but does not explicitly model 'humility in the face of criticism' as the defining characteristic of good leadership.
